```ts
import {
  TLS_VERSION_13, TlsClientHelloView, tlsCopyWindow, tlsEncodeServerHello,
  tlsReadClientHello, tlsWindowHasU16
} from "nish/net/tls/codec";

// `body` is a ClientHello without its four-byte handshake header;
// `random`, `suite` and `x25519Public` are the server's own.
const hello = new TlsClientHelloView()
tlsReadClientHello(hello, body, 0, toI32(body.length))
if (hello.alert !== 0) {
  // send hello.alert, such as TLS_ALERT_DECODE_ERROR (50), and close
} else if (tlsWindowHasU16(hello.data, hello.versionsAt, hello.versionsLength, TLS_VERSION_13)) {
  const sessionId: u8[] = tlsCopyWindow(hello.data, hello.sessionIdAt, hello.sessionIdLength)
  const reply: u8[] = tlsEncodeServerHello(random, sessionId, suite, x25519Public)
}
```

Writes the bytes the lowercase hex constant `text` spells at `out[at]` and answers where they end: how this stack's fixed values, written out where they are defined, become bytes without an array of their own.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsListHas" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlslisthas">

Whether `list` holds `value`.

<scalar-card title="tlsParseClientHello" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsparseclienthello">

Reads the ClientHello body `data[off .. off + len)` — the message without its four-byte handshake header — into a fresh `TlsClientHello`, with `tlsReadClientHello`'s checks and its `alert`, every field copied out.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsReadCertificate" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsreadcertificate">

Reads a server's Certificate body (§4.4.2) into `view`: the request context's length, which the client requires to be 0, and the list of entries.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsReadCertificateVerify" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsreadcertificateverify">

Reads a CertificateVerify body (§4.4.3) into `view`: the scheme and the signature, neither of them checked here.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsReadClientHello" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsreadclienthello">

Reads the ClientHello body `data[off .. off + len)` — the message without its four-byte handshake header — into `hello`, which forgets the last one first.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsReadEncryptedExtensions" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsreadencryptedextensions">

Reads an EncryptedExtensions body (§4.3.1) into `view`: ALPN, an empty `server_name` and `supported_groups` may be there, and any other extension sets `extensionAlert`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsReadNewSessionTicket" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsreadnewsessionticket">

Checks a NewSessionTicket body's structure (§4.6.1) into `view`'s `alert`: the client keeps no tickets, so it reads one only to discard it, but a malformed one is still `decode_error`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsReadServerHello" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsreadserverhello">

Reads the ServerHello body `data[off .. off + len)` — without its handshake header — into `view`, which tells a HelloRetryRequest from it by its `random` (§4.1.3).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsSelectPskIdentity" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsselectpskidentity">

Points `hello`'s `pskIdentity*`, `pskTicketAge` and `pskBinder*` at the offer's identity number `index` and the binder of the same number, and answers whether there is one: false for an index out of range, or a hello that offered no `pre_shared_key` or did not parse.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsServerHelloDowngrade" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlsserverhellodowngrade">

Whether the ServerHello in `view` carries a downgrade sentinel in the last 8 bytes of its random (§4.1.3), which a TLS 1.3 client must refuse with `illegal_parameter`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWindowHasU16" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswindowhasu16">

Whether the 16-bit values `data[at .. at + length)` hold `value`: how a server asks a `TlsClientHelloView`'s windows what it offers without copying them.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWindowString" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswindowstring">

The bytes of `data[at .. at + length)` as a string of one character a byte: ASCII here, a host name.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteCertificate" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswritecertificate">

Writes a server's Certificate (§4.4.2) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends: an empty request context, then each DER certificate of `chain`, leaf first, with no extensions of its own.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteCertificateVerify" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswritecertificateverify">

Writes a CertificateVerify (§4.4.3) at `out[at]`: the signature scheme and the signature as it goes on the wire.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteCertificateVerifyContent" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswritecertificateverifycontent">

Writes what a server's CertificateVerify signs (§4.4.3) at `out[at]`: 64 spaces, the context string "TLS 1.3, server CertificateVerify", a zero byte, and the transcript hash `transcriptHash[off .. off + len)` through Certificate.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteClientHello" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswriteclienthello">

Writes a ClientHello (§4.1.2) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends: `random`, the `legacy_session_id` `sessionId`, the cipher suites `suites`, null compression, then the extensions `server_name` (a `host_name`, left out when `serverName` is empty), `supported_groups` (`groups`), `signature_algorithms`, ALPN (left out when `alpn` is empty), `supported_versions` (TLS 1.3 alone), a `key_share` with the one entry `shareGroup`/`sharePublic`, and `cookie` when `cookie` is not empty (the echo of a HelloRetryRequest's, §4.2.2).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteEncryptedExtensions" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswriteencryptedextensions">

Writes EncryptedExtensions (§4.3.1) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteFinished" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswritefinished">

Writes a Finished (§4.4.4) at `out[at]`, carrying `verifyData[off .. off + len)`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteHelloRetryRequest" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswritehelloretryrequest">

Writes a HelloRetryRequest (§4.1.4) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends: a ServerHello whose `random` is the fixed HelloRetryRequest value, choosing `suite`, echoing the session id, and asking for a share of `group` in `key_share`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteNewSessionTicket" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswritenewsessionticket">

Writes a NewSessionTicket (§4.6.1) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends: `lifetime` in seconds, `ageAdd`, the nonce `nonce[nonceOff .. nonceOff + nonceLength)`, the ticket `ticket[ticketOff .. ticketOff + ticketLength)`, and `extra` as the extensions, encoded by the caller and written as they are.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteServerHello" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswriteserverhello">

Writes a ServerHello (§4.1.3) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends: choosing `suite` and TLS 1.3, echoing the session id `sessionId[sessionIdOff .. sessionIdOff + sessionIdLength)`, and carrying the server's x25519 share.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="tlsWriteServerHelloPsk" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#tlswriteserverhellopsk">

Writes the ServerHello of a resumed handshake (§4.1.3, §4.2.11) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends: `tlsWriteServerHello`'s, with a `pre_shared_key` that names the client's identity number `selectedIdentity` (a `uint16`) ahead of `key_share`, since the server resumes only in `psk_dhe_ke` and so always sends its share.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="TlsClientHello" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#tlsclienthello">

A ClientHello as `tlsParseClientHello` read it (RFC 8446 §4.1.2), each field copied out of the message into an array of its own: the same hello as a `TlsClientHelloView`, for a caller that wants values rather than windows.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="TlsClientHelloView" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#tlsclienthelloview">

A ClientHello as `tlsReadClientHello` read it, without a byte copied: every field the server needs is a window `(…At, …Length)` into `data`, the buffer the hello was read from, and the rest are numbers and flags.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="TlsServerFlightView" icon="phosphor/regular/cube" href="#tlsserverflightview">

One message of the server's flight as a `tlsRead*` function below read it: a ServerHello or HelloRetryRequest, EncryptedExtensions, Certificate, CertificateVerify or NewSessionTicket.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-detail title="One reader and eight writers">

`tlsParseClientHello` reads a ClientHello
body into a `TlsClientHello`, checking its structure: every length against
the bytes it claims, every vector against its RFC 8446 bounds, and no
extension twice (§4.2). A message that breaks one answers the alert a server
sends for it in the hello's `alert` field (`decode_error` for a malformed or
truncated one, `illegal_parameter` for a duplicate), never a panic, since
every byte of it is the peer's. What the fields *mean* — which version,
which suite, whether a share is missing — is the server's to decide, in
`nish/net/tls`.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Reading without copying">

`tlsReadClientHello` is the same reader for a
server that keeps its state in a slot: it reads into a `TlsClientHelloView`
made once, whose fields are windows into the message rather than copies of
it, so a ClientHello read allocates nothing, and `tlsParseClientHello`
copies a view's windows out.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="The writers trust their inputs">

Each answers one whole handshake
message, header included: ServerHello, a resumed ServerHello that names the
PSK it accepts, HelloRetryRequest, EncryptedExtensions, Certificate,
CertificateVerify, Finished and NewSessionTicket. Their inputs come from the
server and the caller's configuration rather than from the peer, so they
check nothing. Each is a `tlsWrite*` function that writes into the caller's
array at an offset — run over an empty array, it measures — and a
`tlsEncode*` one that answers the message in a fresh array.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="The client's side is the mirror">

`tlsWriteClientHello` and
`tlsEncodeClientHello` write the hello `nish/net/tls/client` sends, and five
readers — `tlsReadServerHello` (a HelloRetryRequest too),
`tlsReadEncryptedExtensions`, `tlsReadCertificate`,
`tlsReadCertificateVerify` and `tlsReadNewSessionTicket` — read the
server's flight into a `TlsServerFlightView` made once, as windows, with
the same checks and the same alerts in its `alert` field. A server's bytes
are the peer's just as a client's are, so these readers never panic either
(the `tls-server-flight` fuzz target).

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Extensions">

The ones read are `server_name` (RFC 6066 §3),
`supported_groups`, `signature_algorithms`, `supported_versions` and
`key_share` (RFC 8446 §4.2), `application_layer_protocol_negotiation`
(RFC 7301 §3.1) and `quic_transport_parameters` (RFC 9001 §8.2), and
`pre_shared_key` and `psk_key_exchange_modes` (RFC 8446 §4.2.11, §4.2.9),
whose identities and binders the reader checks against their syntax but
does not open: a ticket and its binder are the server's to judge. Every
other extension is skipped, which is what RFC 8446 §4.2 asks of a server
that does not know it.

</scalar-detail>

Written from the RFCs, not ported from another implementation. Private
names carry the `tls` prefix because a `std/` module's private functions
share the importing program's flat symbol namespace (`docs/wp26-stdlib.md`
§3e).

## tlsCertificateVerifyContent

What a server's CertificateVerify signs (§4.4.3), in a fresh array
(`tlsWriteCertificateVerifyContent`).

```ts
function tlsCertificateVerifyContent(
  transcriptHash: u8[],
): u8[]
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="transcriptHash" type="u8[]" required>

The whole transcript hash through the server's Certificate.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

The content to sign: 98 bytes of prefix, then the hash. It has no handshake header.

</scalar-field>

## tlsClientOffersScheme

Whether `scheme` is one the client's `signature_algorithms` offers, the
only ones a server's CertificateVerify may use (§4.4.3).

```ts
function tlsClientOffersScheme(
  scheme: i32,
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="scheme" type="i32" required>

The scheme a server's CertificateVerify names.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

true for ECDSA P-256 or P-384, or RSA-PSS (rsae) with SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512.

</scalar-field>

## tlsCopyCertificates

The DER certificates of the Certificate `tlsReadCertificate` last read into
`view`, leaf first, each a fresh array.

```ts
function tlsCopyCertificates(
  view: TlsServerFlightView,
): u8[][]
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="view" type="TlsServerFlightView" required>

A view `tlsReadCertificate` has just read into.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[][]">

The chain, copied out of `view.data`; empty if the read failed or another message was read since.

</scalar-field>

## tlsCopyWindow

A copy of `data[at .. at + length)`, which is how a window of a view becomes
an array of its own that outlives the buffer it was read from.

```ts
function tlsCopyWindow(
  data: u8[],
  at: i32,
  length: i32,
): u8[]
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="data" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer the window points into.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

Where the window starts in `data`, in bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="length" type="i32" required>

How many bytes to copy; a negative one copies none.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

A fresh array of `length` bytes; nothing from outside `data` is copied into it.

</scalar-field>

## tlsEncodeCertificate

A server's Certificate (§4.4.2) in a fresh array (`tlsWriteCertificate`).

```ts
function tlsEncodeCertificate(chain: u8[][]): u8[]
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="chain" type="u8[][]" required>

The DER certificates, leaf first, each written as it is.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

The whole message, handshake header included.

</scalar-field>

## tlsEncodeCertificateVerify

A CertificateVerify (§4.4.3) in a fresh array (`tlsWriteCertificateVerify`).

## tlsEncodeClientHello

A ClientHello (§4.1.2) in a fresh array (`tlsWriteClientHello`).

```ts
function tlsEncodeClientHello(
  random: u8[],
  sessionId: u8[],
  suites: i32[],
  groups: i32[],
  shareGroup: i32,
  sharePublic: u8[],
  serverName: string,
  alpn: string[],
  cookie: u8[],
): u8[]
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="random" type="u8[]" required>

The client's 32-byte `random` (§4.1.2), written as it is.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="sessionId" type="u8[]" required>

The `legacy_session_id`, 0 to 32 bytes; the client sends 32 for middlebox compatibility.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="suites" type="i32[]" required>

The cipher suites offered, in order of preference.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="groups" type="i32[]" required>

The groups `supported_groups` offers, in order of preference.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="shareGroup" type="i32" required>

The group of the one key share sent, such as `TLS_GROUP_X25519`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="sharePublic" type="u8[]" required>

That share's public key, its `key_exchange`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="serverName" type="string" required>

The host name for `server_name`, ASCII; empty to leave the extension out.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="alpn" type="string[]" required>

The ALPN protocols offered, one character a byte, in order; empty to leave ALPN out.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="cookie" type="u8[]" required>

A HelloRetryRequest's `cookie` to echo; empty to send none.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

The whole message, handshake header included.

</scalar-field>

## tlsEncodeEncryptedExtensions

EncryptedExtensions (§4.3.1) in a fresh array (`tlsWriteEncryptedExtensions`),
the ALPN protocol given as its bytes.

```ts
function tlsEncodeEncryptedExtensions(
  extra: u8[],
  alpn: u8[],
  acknowledgeServerName: boolean,
  quicTransportParameters: u8[] | null,
): u8[]
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="extra" type="u8[]" required>

Whole extensions, type and length included, written first and unchecked; empty for none.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="alpn" type="u8[]" required>

The protocol the server chose, as its bytes, at most 255; empty to send no ALPN.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="acknowledgeServerName" type="boolean" required>

Whether to send the empty `server_name` that says the server used the name.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="quicTransportParameters" type="u8[] | null" required>

The server's QUIC transport parameters, opaque; `null` to send none.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

The whole message, handshake header included.

</scalar-field>

## tlsEncodeFinished

A Finished (§4.4.4) carrying `verifyData`, in a fresh array (`tlsWriteFinished`).

```ts
function tlsEncodeFinished(verifyData: u8[]): u8[]
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="verifyData" type="u8[]" required>

The whole `verify_data`, the HMAC the key schedule computed: 32 or 48 bytes.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

The whole message, handshake header included.

</scalar-field>

## tlsEncodeHelloRetryRequest

A HelloRetryRequest (§4.1.4) choosing `suite`, echoing `sessionId` and
asking for `group`, in a fresh array (`tlsWriteHelloRetryRequest`).

```ts
function tlsEncodeHelloRetryRequest(
  sessionId: u8[],
  suite: i32,
  group: i32,
): u8[]
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="sessionId" type="u8[]" required>

The client's whole `legacy_session_id`, 0 to 32 bytes, echoed.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="suite" type="i32" required>

The cipher suite the server chose, which the second ServerHello must choose again.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="group" type="i32" required>

The group the client is asked to send a share for, such as `TLS_GROUP_X25519`.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

The whole message, handshake header included.

</scalar-field>

## tlsEncodeNewSessionTicket

A NewSessionTicket (§4.6.1) in a fresh array (`tlsWriteNewSessionTicket`).

```ts
function tlsEncodeNewSessionTicket(
  lifetime: u32,
  ageAdd: u32,
  nonce: u8[],
  ticket: u8[],
  extra: u8[],
): u8[]
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="lifetime" type="u32" required>

How long the ticket may be used, in seconds; RFC 8446 §4.6.1 caps it at seven days.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ageAdd" type="u32" required>

The `ticket_age_add` that obfuscates the ticket age, which §4.6.1 wants fresh and random.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="nonce" type="u8[]" required>

The whole `ticket_nonce`, 0 to 255 bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ticket" type="u8[]" required>

The whole ticket the client will send back: §4.6.1 allows 1 to 65535 bytes, not checked here.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="extra" type="u8[]" required>

Whole extensions, type and length included, written unchecked; empty for none.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

The whole message, handshake header included.

</scalar-field>

## tlsEncodeServerHello

A ServerHello (§4.1.3) choosing `suite` and TLS 1.3, echoing the client's
`sessionId`, and carrying the server's x25519 share, in a fresh array
(`tlsWriteServerHello`).

```ts
function tlsEncodeServerHello(
  random: u8[],
  sessionId: u8[],
  suite: i32,
  x25519Public: u8[],
): u8[]
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="random" type="u8[]" required>

The server's 32-byte `random` (§4.1.3), written as it is.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="sessionId" type="u8[]" required>

The client's whole `legacy_session_id`, 0 to 32 bytes, echoed.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="suite" type="i32" required>

The cipher suite the server chose.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="x25519Public" type="u8[]" required>

The server's x25519 public key, the share's `key_exchange`.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="u8[]">

The whole message, handshake header included.

</scalar-field>

## tlsEncodeServerHelloPsk

A resumed handshake's ServerHello naming `selectedIdentity`, in a fresh
array (`tlsWriteServerHelloPsk`).

```ts
function tlsEncodeServerHelloPsk(
  random: u8[],
  sessionId: u8[],
  suite: i32,
  x25519Public: u8[],
  selectedIdentity: i32,
): u8[]
```

<scalar-field name="random" type="u8[]" required>

The server's 32-byte `random` (§4.1.3), written as it is.

</scalar-field>

The client's whole `legacy_session_id`, 0 to 32 bytes, echoed.

</scalar-field>

The cipher suite the server chose.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="x25519Public" type="u8[]" required>

The server's x25519 public key, the share's `key_exchange`.

</scalar-field>

The index, from 0, of the client's PSK identity the server accepts; only its low

</scalar-field>

## tlsHexInto

Writes the bytes the lowercase hex constant `text` spells at `out[at]` and
answers where they end: how this stack's fixed values, written out where
they are defined, become bytes without an array of their own.

```ts
function tlsHexInto(
  text: string,
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="text" type="string" required>

Lowercase hex digits, two a byte; a last odd digit is ignored, and nothing else is checked.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array to write into; a byte that would land outside it is dropped.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

Where the first byte goes in `out`.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

`at` plus the number of bytes `text` spells, written or not.

</scalar-field>

## tlsListHas

Whether `list` holds `value`.

```ts
function tlsListHas(
  list: i32[],
  value: i32,
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="list" type="i32[]" required>

The values to look in, such as a `TlsClientHello`'s `cipherSuites` or `groups`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="value" type="i32" required>

The code point to look for, such as a suite or a group.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

true when `value` is somewhere in `list`.

</scalar-field>

## tlsParseClientHello

Reads the ClientHello body `data[off .. off + len)` — the message without
its four-byte handshake header — into a fresh `TlsClientHello`, with
`tlsReadClientHello`'s checks and its `alert`, every field copied out.

```ts
function tlsParseClientHello(
  data: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
): TlsClientHello
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="data" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer that holds the message; nothing in the answer points into it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where the body starts in `data`, in bytes, just past the handshake header.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="len" type="i32" required>

How many bytes the body is, from `off`.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="TlsClientHello">

A fresh hello whose `alert` is 0 when the body parsed, or the alert it earns.

</scalar-field>

## tlsReadCertificate

Reads a server's Certificate body (§4.4.2) into `view`: the request
context's length, which the client requires to be 0, and the list of
entries. An empty list is `decode_error`, as §4.4.2.4 has a client answer
it; an entry with extensions is `unsupported_extension`, because the
client offers none that a CertificateEntry may carry.

```ts
function tlsReadCertificate(
  view: TlsServerFlightView,
  data: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
): void
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="view" type="TlsServerFlightView" required>

The view to read into, cleared first; its `alert` and `extensionAlert` are the verdicts.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="data" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer that holds the message, which the view's windows then point into.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where the Certificate body starts in `data`, in bytes, just past the handshake header.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="len" type="i32" required>

How many bytes the body is, from `off`.

</scalar-field>

## tlsReadCertificateVerify

Reads a CertificateVerify body (§4.4.3) into `view`: the scheme and the
signature, neither of them checked here.

```ts
function tlsReadCertificateVerify(
  view: TlsServerFlightView,
  data: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
): void
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="view" type="TlsServerFlightView" required>

The view to read into, cleared first; its `alert` and `extensionAlert` are the verdicts.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="data" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer that holds the message, which the view's windows then point into.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where the CertificateVerify body starts in `data`, in bytes, just past the handshake header.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="len" type="i32" required>

How many bytes the body is, from `off`.

</scalar-field>

## tlsReadClientHello

Reads the ClientHello body `data[off .. off + len)` — the message without
its four-byte handshake header — into `hello`, which forgets the last one
first. Its `alert` is 0 when the body parsed; otherwise the first fault
decides it: `decode_error` for a length past its bytes, a vector out of its
bounds or bytes left over, and `illegal_parameter` for an extension sent
twice (§4.2), a `pre_shared_key` that is not the last extension (§4.2.11),
two shares for one group, or a bad `server_name`. A window outside `data`
is `decode_error` too, rather than a panic. A hello that parses but offers
`pre_shared_key` with a different number of identities and binders is
`illegal_parameter`, and one that offers it without
`psk_key_exchange_modes` is `missing_extension` (§4.2.9): rows 10 to 13 of
the fallback table in `docs/security/tls.md`, "Resumption". Nothing is copied: the windows
point into `data`, which must outlive the use made of them.

```ts
function tlsReadClientHello(
  hello: TlsClientHelloView,
  data: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
): void
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="hello" type="TlsClientHelloView" required>

The view to read into, cleared first; its `alert` is the verdict.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="data" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer that holds the message, which the view's windows then point into.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where the body starts in `data`, in bytes, just past the handshake header.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="len" type="i32" required>

How many bytes the body is, from `off`.

</scalar-field>

## tlsReadEncryptedExtensions

Reads an EncryptedExtensions body (§4.3.1) into `view`: ALPN, an empty
`server_name` and `supported_groups` may be there, and any other extension
sets `extensionAlert`.

```ts
function tlsReadEncryptedExtensions(
  view: TlsServerFlightView,
  data: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
): void
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="view" type="TlsServerFlightView" required>

The view to read into, cleared first; its `alert` and `extensionAlert` are the verdicts.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="data" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer that holds the message, which the view's windows then point into.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where the EncryptedExtensions body starts in `data`, in bytes, just past the handshake header.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="len" type="i32" required>

How many bytes the body is, from `off`.

</scalar-field>

## tlsReadNewSessionTicket

Checks a NewSessionTicket body's structure (§4.6.1) into `view`'s `alert`:
the client keeps no tickets, so it reads one only to discard it, but a
malformed one is still `decode_error`.

```ts
function tlsReadNewSessionTicket(
  view: TlsServerFlightView,
  data: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
): void
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="view" type="TlsServerFlightView" required>

The view to read into, cleared first; its `alert` and `extensionAlert` are the verdicts.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="data" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer that holds the message, which the view's windows then point into.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where the NewSessionTicket body starts in `data`, in bytes, just past the handshake header.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="len" type="i32" required>

How many bytes the body is, from `off`.

</scalar-field>

## tlsReadServerHello

Reads the ServerHello body `data[off .. off + len)` — without its handshake
header — into `view`, which tells a HelloRetryRequest from it by its
`random` (§4.1.3). An absent extensions block parses: it is how a TLS 1.2
or older server answers, which the client refuses for its version.

```ts
function tlsReadServerHello(
  view: TlsServerFlightView,
  data: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
): void
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="view" type="TlsServerFlightView" required>

The view to read into, cleared first; its `alert` and `extensionAlert` are the verdicts.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="data" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer that holds the message, which the view's windows then point into.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where the ServerHello body starts in `data`, in bytes, just past the handshake header.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="len" type="i32" required>

How many bytes the body is, from `off`.

</scalar-field>

## tlsSelectPskIdentity

Points `hello`'s `pskIdentity*`, `pskTicketAge` and `pskBinder*` at the
offer's identity number `index` and the binder of the same number, and
answers whether there is one: false for an index out of range, or a hello
that offered no `pre_shared_key` or did not parse. It walks the lists
`tlsReadClientHello` checked, and allocates nothing.

```ts
function tlsSelectPskIdentity(
  hello: TlsClientHelloView,
  index: i32,
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="hello" type="TlsClientHelloView" required>

A view `tlsReadClientHello` has read into; its PSK windows are cleared first either way.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="index" type="i32" required>

Which identity to choose, from 0, in the client's order.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

true when the identity and its binder were found and the windows point at them.

</scalar-field>

## tlsServerHelloDowngrade

Whether the ServerHello in `view` carries a downgrade sentinel in the last
8 bytes of its random (§4.1.3), which a TLS 1.3 client must refuse with
`illegal_parameter`.

```ts
function tlsServerHelloDowngrade(
  view: TlsServerFlightView,
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="view" type="TlsServerFlightView" required>

A view `tlsReadServerHello` has just read into.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

true when the random ends in the TLS 1.2 or the TLS 1.1 sentinel.

</scalar-field>

## tlsWindowHasU16

Whether the 16-bit values `data[at .. at + length)` hold `value`: how a
server asks a `TlsClientHelloView`'s windows what it offers without copying
them. The values are big-endian pairs; a last odd byte, and any part of the
window outside `data`, is not read.

```ts
function tlsWindowHasU16(
  data: u8[],
  at: i32,
  length: i32,
  value: i32,
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="data" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer the window points into, such as a view's `data`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

Where the window starts in `data`, in bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="length" type="i32" required>

How many bytes the window holds, two a value.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="value" type="i32" required>

The 16-bit code point to look for, such as `TLS_VERSION_13`.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

true when one of the window's values is `value`.

</scalar-field>

## tlsWindowString

The bytes of `data[at .. at + length)` as a string of one character a byte:
ASCII here, a host name.

```ts
function tlsWindowString(
  data: u8[],
  at: i32,
  length: i32,
): string
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="data" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer the window points into.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

Where the window starts in `data`, in bytes.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="length" type="i32" required>

How many bytes the window holds; any part outside `data` is left out.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

A fresh string, one character for each byte read.

</scalar-field>

## tlsWriteCertificate

Writes a server's Certificate (§4.4.2) at `out[at]` and answers where it
ends: an empty request context, then each DER certificate of `chain`, leaf
first, with no extensions of its own.

```ts
function tlsWriteCertificate(
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
  chain: u8[][],
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array to write into; a byte that would land outside it is dropped, so an empty one measures.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

Where the message, handshake header first, starts in `out`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="chain" type="u8[][]" required>

The DER certificates, leaf first, each written as it is.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

Where the message ends in `out`: `at` plus its length, written or not.

</scalar-field>

## tlsWriteCertificateVerify

Writes a CertificateVerify (§4.4.3) at `out[at]`: the signature scheme and
the signature as it goes on the wire.

```ts
function tlsWriteCertificateVerify(
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
  scheme: i32,
  signature: u8[],
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array to write into; a byte that would land outside it is dropped, so an empty one measures.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

Where the message, handshake header first, starts in `out`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="scheme" type="i32" required>

The signature scheme, such as `TLS_SIGNATURE_ECDSA_SECP256R1_SHA256`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="signature" type="u8[]" required>

The signature over `tlsCertificateVerifyContent`, in the scheme's wire encoding.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

Where the message ends in `out`: `at` plus its length, written or not.

</scalar-field>

## tlsWriteCertificateVerifyContent

Writes what a server's CertificateVerify signs (§4.4.3) at `out[at]`: 64
spaces, the context string "TLS 1.3, server CertificateVerify", a zero byte,
and the transcript hash `transcriptHash[off .. off + len)` through
Certificate.

```ts
function tlsWriteCertificateVerifyContent(
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
  transcriptHash: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array to write into; a byte that would land outside it is dropped, so an empty one measures.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

Where the content starts in `out`. It has no handshake header: it is signed, not sent.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="transcriptHash" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer that holds the transcript hash through the server's Certificate.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where the hash starts in `transcriptHash`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="len" type="i32" required>

How many bytes the hash is: the suite's hash length.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

Where the content ends in `out`: `at` plus 98 plus `len`, written or not.

</scalar-field>

## tlsWriteClientHello

Writes a ClientHello (§4.1.2) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends:
`random`, the `legacy_session_id` `sessionId`, the cipher suites `suites`,
null compression, then the extensions `server_name` (a `host_name`, left
out when `serverName` is empty), `supported_groups` (`groups`),
`signature_algorithms`, ALPN (left out when `alpn` is empty),
`supported_versions` (TLS 1.3 alone), a `key_share` with the one entry
`shareGroup`/`sharePublic`, and `cookie` when `cookie` is not empty (the
echo of a HelloRetryRequest's, §4.2.2).

```ts
function tlsWriteClientHello(
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
  random: u8[],
  sessionId: u8[],
  suites: i32[],
  groups: i32[],
  shareGroup: i32,
  sharePublic: u8[],
  serverName: string,
  alpn: string[],
  cookie: u8[],
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array to write into; a byte that would land outside it is dropped, so an empty one measures.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

Where the message, handshake header first, starts in `out`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="random" type="u8[]" required>

The client's 32-byte `random` (§4.1.2), written as it is.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="sessionId" type="u8[]" required>

The `legacy_session_id`, 0 to 32 bytes; the client sends 32 for middlebox compatibility.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="suites" type="i32[]" required>

The cipher suites offered, in order of preference.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="groups" type="i32[]" required>

The groups `supported_groups` offers, in order of preference.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="shareGroup" type="i32" required>

The group of the one key share sent, such as `TLS_GROUP_X25519`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="sharePublic" type="u8[]" required>

That share's public key, its `key_exchange`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="serverName" type="string" required>

The host name for `server_name`, ASCII; empty to leave the extension out.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="alpn" type="string[]" required>

The ALPN protocols offered, one character a byte, in order; empty to leave ALPN out.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="cookie" type="u8[]" required>

A HelloRetryRequest's `cookie` to echo; empty to send none.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

Where the message ends in `out`: `at` plus its length, written or not.

</scalar-field>

## tlsWriteEncryptedExtensions

Writes EncryptedExtensions (§4.3.1) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends.
`extra` is extensions the caller encodes itself, written first and as they
are; then the chosen ALPN protocol when `alpn` is not empty (RFC 7301 §3.1,
a list of exactly one), an empty `server_name` when `acknowledgeServerName`
(RFC 6066 §3's acknowledgement), and the server's
`quic_transport_parameters` when `quicTransportParameters` is not `null`.

```ts
function tlsWriteEncryptedExtensions(
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
  extra: u8[],
  alpn: string,
  acknowledgeServerName: boolean,
  quicTransportParameters: u8[] | null,
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array to write into; a byte that would land outside it is dropped, so an empty one measures.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

Where the message, handshake header first, starts in `out`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="extra" type="u8[]" required>

Whole extensions, type and length included, written first and unchecked; empty for none.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="alpn" type="string" required>

The protocol the server chose, one character a byte, at most 255; empty to send no ALPN.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="acknowledgeServerName" type="boolean" required>

Whether to send the empty `server_name` that says the server used the name.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="quicTransportParameters" type="u8[] | null" required>

The server's QUIC transport parameters, opaque; `null` to send none.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

Where the message ends in `out`: `at` plus its length, written or not.

</scalar-field>

## tlsWriteFinished

Writes a Finished (§4.4.4) at `out[at]`, carrying `verifyData[off .. off + len)`.

```ts

```

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array to write into; a byte that would land outside it is dropped, so an empty one measures.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

Where the message, handshake header first, starts in `out`.

</scalar-field>

The buffer that holds the `verify_data`, the HMAC the key schedule computed.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where the `verify_data` starts in `verifyData`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="len" type="i32" required>

How many bytes it is: the suite's hash length, 32 or 48.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

Where the message ends in `out`: `at` plus its length, written or not.

</scalar-field>

## tlsWriteHelloRetryRequest

Writes a HelloRetryRequest (§4.1.4) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends:
a ServerHello whose `random` is the fixed HelloRetryRequest value, choosing
`suite`, echoing the session id, and asking for a share of `group` in
`key_share`. No cookie is sent.

```ts
function tlsWriteHelloRetryRequest(
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
  sessionId: u8[],
  sessionIdOff: i32,
  sessionIdLength: i32,
  suite: i32,
  group: i32,
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array to write into; a byte that would land outside it is dropped, so an empty one measures.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

Where the message, handshake header first, starts in `out`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="sessionId" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer that holds the client's `legacy_session_id`, such as the hello's `data`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="sessionIdOff" type="i32" required>

Where the session id starts in `sessionId`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="sessionIdLength" type="i32" required>

How many bytes the session id is, 0 to 32.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="suite" type="i32" required>

The cipher suite the server chose, which the second ServerHello must choose again.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="group" type="i32" required>

The group the client is asked to send a share for, such as `TLS_GROUP_X25519`.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

Where the message ends in `out`: `at` plus its length, written or not.

</scalar-field>

## tlsWriteNewSessionTicket

Writes a NewSessionTicket (§4.6.1) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends:
`lifetime` in seconds, `ageAdd`, the nonce
`nonce[nonceOff .. nonceOff + nonceLength)`, the ticket
`ticket[ticketOff .. ticketOff + ticketLength)`, and `extra` as the
extensions, encoded by the caller and written as they are. The server sends
none; RFC 8448 §3's ticket carries `early_data`.

```ts
function tlsWriteNewSessionTicket(
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
  lifetime: u32,
  ageAdd: u32,
  nonce: u8[],
  nonceOff: i32,
  nonceLength: i32,
  ticket: u8[],
  ticketOff: i32,
  ticketLength: i32,
  extra: u8[],
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array to write into; a byte that would land outside it is dropped, so an empty one measures.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

Where the message, handshake header first, starts in `out`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="lifetime" type="u32" required>

How long the ticket may be used, in seconds; RFC 8446 §4.6.1 caps it at seven days.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ageAdd" type="u32" required>

The `ticket_age_add` that obfuscates the ticket age, which §4.6.1 wants fresh and random.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="nonce" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer that holds the `ticket_nonce`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="nonceOff" type="i32" required>

Where the nonce starts in `nonce`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="nonceLength" type="i32" required>

How many bytes the nonce is, 0 to 255.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ticket" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer that holds the ticket the client will send back.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ticketOff" type="i32" required>

Where the ticket starts in `ticket`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ticketLength" type="i32" required>

How many bytes the ticket is: §4.6.1 allows 1 to 65535, not checked here.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="extra" type="u8[]" required>

Whole extensions, type and length included, written unchecked; empty for none.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

Where the message ends in `out`: `at` plus its length, written or not.

</scalar-field>

## tlsWriteServerHello

Writes a ServerHello (§4.1.3) at `out[at]` and answers where it ends:
choosing `suite` and TLS 1.3, echoing the session id
`sessionId[sessionIdOff .. sessionIdOff + sessionIdLength)`, and carrying
the server's x25519 share. The extensions are `key_share` then
`supported_versions`, the order RFC 8448 §3 shows.

```ts
function tlsWriteServerHello(
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
  random: u8[],
  sessionId: u8[],
  sessionIdOff: i32,
  sessionIdLength: i32,
  suite: i32,
  x25519Public: u8[],
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array to write into; a byte that would land outside it is dropped, so an empty one measures.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

Where the message, handshake header first, starts in `out`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="random" type="u8[]" required>

The server's 32-byte `random` (§4.1.3), written as it is.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="sessionId" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer that holds the client's `legacy_session_id`, such as the hello's `data`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="sessionIdOff" type="i32" required>

Where the session id starts in `sessionId`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="sessionIdLength" type="i32" required>

How many bytes the session id is, 0 to 32.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="suite" type="i32" required>

The cipher suite the server chose, such as `nish/net/tls/schedule`'s `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="x25519Public" type="u8[]" required>

The server's x25519 public key, the share's `key_exchange`.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

Where the message ends in `out`: `at` plus its length, written or not.

</scalar-field>

## tlsWriteServerHelloPsk

Writes the ServerHello of a resumed handshake (§4.1.3, §4.2.11) at
`out[at]` and answers where it ends: `tlsWriteServerHello`'s, with a
`pre_shared_key` that names the client's identity number
`selectedIdentity` (a `uint16`) ahead of `key_share`, since the server
resumes only in `psk_dhe_ke` and so always sends its share.

```ts
function tlsWriteServerHelloPsk(
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
  random: u8[],
  sessionId: u8[],
  sessionIdOff: i32,
  sessionIdLength: i32,
  suite: i32,
  x25519Public: u8[],
  selectedIdentity: i32,
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The array to write into; a byte that would land outside it is dropped, so an empty one measures.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

Where the message, handshake header first, starts in `out`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="random" type="u8[]" required>

The server's 32-byte `random` (§4.1.3), written as it is.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="sessionId" type="u8[]" required>

The buffer that holds the client's `legacy_session_id`, such as the hello's `data`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="sessionIdOff" type="i32" required>

Where the session id starts in `sessionId`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="sessionIdLength" type="i32" required>

How many bytes the session id is, 0 to 32.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="suite" type="i32" required>

The cipher suite the server chose.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="x25519Public" type="u8[]" required>

The server's x25519 public key, the share's `key_exchange`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="selectedIdentity" type="i32" required>

The index, from 0, of the client's PSK identity the server accepts; only its low
  16 bits are written.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

Where the message ends in `out`: `at` plus its length, written or not.

</scalar-field>

## TlsClientHello

A ClientHello as `tlsParseClientHello` read it (RFC 8446 §4.1.2), each field
copied out of the message into an array of its own: the same hello as a
`TlsClientHelloView`, for a caller that wants values rather than windows. A
field whose extension was absent keeps its empty value, and its `has*` flag
says so.

```ts
class TlsClientHello
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TlsClientHello()` | Makes an empty hello, every field empty and every flag false, for `tlsParseClientHello` to fill. |
| `alert: i32` | 0 when the message parsed, or the alert it earns: `decode_error` or `illegal_parameter`. |
| `alpn: u8[][]` | The ALPN protocol names offered, each as its bytes (RFC 7301 §3.1). |
| `cipherSuites: i32[]` |  |
| `extensionTypes: i32[]` | Every extension type read, in order. |
| `groups: i32[]` | `supported_groups`, in the client's order. |
| `hasAlpn: boolean` |  |
| `hasKeyShare: boolean` |  |
| `hasPreSharedKey: boolean` |  |
| `hasPskModes: boolean` |  |
| `hasQuicTransportParameters: boolean` |  |
| `hasServerName: boolean` |  |
| `hasSignatureAlgorithms: boolean` |  |
| `hasSupportedGroups: boolean` |  |
| `hasSupportedVersions: boolean` |  |
| `hasX25519Share: boolean` |  |
| `legacyVersion: i32` |  |
| `nullCompressionOnly: boolean` | Whether `legacy_compression_methods` is the single null method TLS 1.3 requires (§4.1.2). |
| `pskBinders: u8[][]` | `pre_shared_key`'s binders, one an identity. |
| `pskBindersPrefix: i32` | How many bytes of the body come before `binders`: the body truncated there, after its handshake header, is what each binder covers (§4.2.11.2). |
| `pskDheKe: boolean` | Whether `psk_key_exchange_modes` lists `psk_dhe_ke`. |
| `pskIdentities: u8[][]` | `pre_shared_key`'s identities, in the client's order, and each one's obfuscated ticket age (§4.2.11). |
| `pskModes: u8[]` | `psk_key_exchange_modes`, one byte a mode. |
| `pskTicketAges: u32[]` |  |
| `quicTransportParameters: u8[]` | The client's `quic_transport_parameters`, opaque (RFC 9001 §8.2). |
| `random: u8[]` |  |
| `serverName: string` | The `host_name` of `server_name`, or empty. |
| `sessionId: u8[]` | `legacy_session_id`, which a server echoes (§4.1.3). |
| `shareGroups: i32[]` | Every group a key share was offered for, in order. |
| `signatureSchemes: i32[]` | `signature_algorithms`, in the client's order. |
| `versions: i32[]` | `supported_versions`, in the client's order. |
| `x25519Share: u8[]` | The x25519 share's key_exchange, as sent; its length is the server's to check. |

## TlsClientHelloView

A ClientHello as `tlsReadClientHello` read it, without a byte copied: every
field the server needs is a window `(…At, …Length)` into `data`, the buffer
the hello was read from, and the rest are numbers and flags. A field whose
extension was absent keeps an empty window, and its `has*` flag says so,
since an empty list and a missing extension mean different things to the
server (§9.2). Make one per connection and read every hello into it: it
allocates nothing after its constructor, so a handshake that keeps its state
in a slot reads its ClientHellos without moving the arena.

```ts
class TlsClientHelloView
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TlsClientHelloView()` | Makes an empty view, every window empty and every flag false, for `tlsReadClientHello` to fill. |
| `alert: i32` | 0 when the message parsed, or the alert it earns: `decode_error` or `illegal_parameter`. |
| `alpnAt: i32` | ALPN's `protocol_name_list`, each name a length byte and its bytes (RFC 7301 §3.1). |
| `alpnLength: i32` |  |
| `extensionsAt: i32` | The extensions block, every extension in it. |
| `extensionsLength: i32` |  |
| `groupsAt: i32` | `supported_groups`, 16-bit values. |
| `groupsLength: i32` |  |
| `hasAlpn: boolean` |  |
| `hasKeyShare: boolean` |  |
| `hasPreSharedKey: boolean` |  |
| `hasPskModes: boolean` |  |
| `hasQuicTransportParameters: boolean` |  |
| `hasServerName: boolean` |  |
| `hasSignatureAlgorithms: boolean` |  |
| `hasSupportedGroups: boolean` |  |
| `hasSupportedVersions: boolean` |  |
| `hasX25519Share: boolean` |  |
| `legacyVersion: i32` |  |
| `nullCompressionOnly: boolean` | Whether `legacy_compression_methods` is the single null method TLS 1.3 requires (§4.1.2). |
| `pskBinderAt: i32` | That identity's binder, the entry of the same index in `binders`. |
| `pskBinderCount: i32` |  |
| `pskBinderLength: i32` |  |
| `pskBindersAt: i32` | `pre_shared_key`'s `binders` list: each a PskBinderEntry<32..255>. |
| `pskBindersLength: i32` |  |
| `pskBindersPrefixAt: i32` | Where `binders`' two-byte length starts: the ClientHello up to here, its handshake header included, is what each binder is computed over (§4.2.11.2). |
| `pskDheKe: boolean` | Whether `ke_modes` lists `psk_dhe_ke`, the one mode the server resumes in. |
| `pskIdentitiesAt: i32` | `pre_shared_key`'s `identities` list (§4.2.11): each an identity<1..2^16-1> and a 32-bit obfuscated age. |
| `pskIdentitiesLength: i32` |  |
| `pskIdentityAt: i32` | The identity `tlsSelectPskIdentity` last chose: its bytes and its obfuscated ticket age. |
| `pskIdentityCount: i32` |  |
| `pskIdentityLength: i32` |  |
| `pskModesAt: i32` | `psk_key_exchange_modes`' `ke_modes`, one byte a mode (§4.2.9). |
| `pskModesLength: i32` |  |
| `pskTicketAge: u32` |  |
| `quicAt: i32` | The client's `quic_transport_parameters`, opaque (RFC 9001 §8.2). |
| `quicLength: i32` |  |
| `randomAt: i32` |  |
| `schemesAt: i32` | `signature_algorithms`, 16-bit values. |
| `schemesLength: i32` |  |
| `serverNameAt: i32` | The `host_name` of `server_name`, or empty. |
| `serverNameLength: i32` |  |
| `sessionIdAt: i32` | `legacy_session_id`, which a server echoes (§4.1.3). |
| `sessionIdLength: i32` |  |
| `sharesAt: i32` | The `client_shares` list of `key_share`, every entry in it. |
| `sharesLength: i32` |  |
| `suitesAt: i32` | `cipher_suites`, 16-bit values in the client's order. |
| `suitesLength: i32` |  |
| `versionsAt: i32` | `supported_versions`, 16-bit values. |
| `versionsLength: i32` |  |
| `x25519ShareAt: i32` | The x25519 share's key_exchange, as sent; its length is the server's to check. |
| `x25519ShareLength: i32` |  |

## TlsServerFlightView

One message of the server's flight as a `tlsRead*` function below read it:
a ServerHello or HelloRetryRequest, EncryptedExtensions, Certificate,
CertificateVerify or NewSessionTicket. Like `TlsClientHelloView` its fields
are windows into `data` and numbers, so a read allocates nothing; each read
forgets the last message first.

Two verdicts, kept apart so the client can rank them. `alert` is the
structure's: `decode_error` for a length past its bytes, a vector out of
its bounds or bytes left over. `extensionAlert` is the extensions': an
extension sent twice, or one the client offered but this message may not
carry, is `illegal_parameter`; one the client never offers is
`unsupported_extension` (§4.2). The client reads the structure first, then
the version and the downgrade sentinel, then the extensions, so that a
TLS 1.2 ServerHello is refused for its version, not for the extensions a
TLS 1.2 server sends.

```ts
class TlsServerFlightView
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new TlsServerFlightView()` | Makes an empty view, every window empty and every flag false, for the `tlsRead*` functions to fill. |
| `alert: i32` | 0 when the message parsed, else `decode_error`. |
| `alpnAt: i32` | EncryptedExtensions' ALPN: the one protocol the server chose (RFC 7301 §3.1). |
| `alpnLength: i32` |  |
| `certificateCount: i32` |  |
| `certificatesAt: i32` | Certificate's `certificate_list`, every entry in it, and how many there are. |
| `certificatesLength: i32` |  |
| `compression: i32` |  |
| `contextLength: i32` | Certificate's `certificate_request_context`, which must be empty for a server's (§4.4.2). |
| `cookieAt: i32` | A HelloRetryRequest's `cookie`, which the second ClientHello echoes (§4.2.2). |
| `cookieLength: i32` |  |
| `extensionAlert: i32` | 0 when the extensions are ones this message may carry, else `illegal_parameter` or `unsupported_extension`. |
| `hasAlpn: boolean` |  |
| `hasCookie: boolean` |  |
| `hasKeyShare: boolean` |  |
| `hasSupportedVersions: boolean` |  |
| `isRetry: boolean` | A ServerHello whose `random` is the HelloRetryRequest value (§4.1.3). |
| `legacyVersion: i32` |  |
| `randomAt: i32` |  |
| `scheme: i32` | CertificateVerify's scheme and signature (§4.4.3). |
| `selectedVersion: i32` |  |
| `serverNameAcknowledged: boolean` | EncryptedExtensions' empty `server_name`, the acknowledgement of RFC 6066 §3. |
| `sessionIdAt: i32` |  |
| `sessionIdLength: i32` |  |
| `shareAt: i32` |  |
| `shareGroup: i32` | `key_share`: a ServerHello's entry, or a HelloRetryRequest's `selected_group` with an empty share. |
| `shareLength: i32` |  |
| `signatureAt: i32` |  |
| `signatureLength: i32` |  |
| `suite: i32` |  |
